flawed_step: Step 3: From a vertex receiving greedy color k, one might claim that its earlier neighbors of greedy colors 1,...,k-1 force chi(G) >= k-1. This is unjustified: those neighbors need not be mutually adjacent and may share colors in an optimal coloring.
counterexample: Let V={r,s,t,u,c,d,e,f} and E={rs,rt,rc,tu,cd,ce,ef}. This graph is a nontrivial tree, so chi(G)=2. In the order s,u,t,d,f,e,c,r, greedy assigns colors 1,1,2,1,1,2,3,4 respectively. Thus it uses 4 colors, exceeding chi(G)+1=3.
assessment_summary: The proposed bound is false. Greedy color classes need not correspond to distinct classes in an optimal coloring; the displayed tree and ordering produce four greedy colors although its chromatic number is two.
